channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: British comedian Russell Brand found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults
item.description: British comedian Russell Brand was on Thursday, November 5, found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults by a London jury, including a 16-year-old girl. He now faces "significant" prison time, according to the judge.

item.title: Pressure mounts on US Defence chief Hegseth after Republican election rout
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is under growing pressure, with victorious Democrats planning to target him in Congress and Republicans blaming the Iran war he championed for their election losses. President Donald Trump has stood by Hegseth so far, insisting he's doing "a very good job". But Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both blamed midterm election losses on the Iran war, for which Hegseth is a key advocate and spokesman.

item.title: 'Trump is a very dangerous person for the world': EU's former top diplomat Josep Borrell
item.description: In an interview with Talking Europe, the EU's former top diplomat Josep Borrell reacts to the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections, warning that US President Donald Trump is still "a very dangerous person for the world".

item.title: Trump moves to make Oval Office a national monument to prevent future major changes
item.description: Trump indicated the proclamation would have to be ratified by Congress.

item.title: 'Chaos within aviation industry' as European air traffic hit by bomb threats
item.description: Officials across Europe reported a fresh slew of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, November 6, following a string of hoaxes that have caused flight diversions this week. Two broadcasters also received security threats, in a possible sign the menace was spreading beyond the skies. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi has more.

item.title: Meghan Markle's father Thomas Markle Sr. arrested by FBI in Florida
item.description: Thomas Markle Sr. moved to Florida after many years in the Philippines.

item.title: 4 Colorado officers shot, 1 fatally, after gunfight with suspect: Police
item.description: The suspect was also killed in the gunfire, a police official said.

item.title: Turkey to push for 'electrification' drive at COP31 as climate threats mount
item.description: COP31 host Turkey is set to push for a "electrification" drive to help meet global elergy demand as the UN climate conference kicks off in Antalya on Monday. The annual summit takes place this year under the shadow of a cost-of-living crisis fuelled by the war in the Middle East.

item.title: Amateur cricketer 'Clicky Pointing' banned for two years over viral cheating
item.description: An amateur cricketer dubbed 'Clicky Pointing' has been banned from the sport for two years over cheating during games.

item.title: European air traffic is targeted by new threats after a week of hoaxes
item.description: Officials across Europe reported a fresh slew of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, following a string of hoaxes that have caused flight diversions this week. Two broadcasters also received security threats. (Image credit: Andreea Alexandru)

item.title: China keeps a close eye on US midterm shake-up
item.description: The US midterm elections have resulted in the Democratic Party taking control of both chambers of the US Congress, leaving Donald Trump as a lame duck president for the remainder of his term. Professor Steve Tsang of the SOAS China Institute tells FRANCE 24 that, while a weakened Trump could strengthen Beijing's negotiating position, the Chinese leadership is aware that Congress has relatively little sway over foreign policy and is keen to maintain warm personal ties between the two presidents.

item.title: Election 2026 live results: Raman promises smooth transition of power to LA mayor
item.description: Raman is poised to become the 44th mayor of the nation’s second-largest city.

item.title: Jobs report shows hiring accelerated in October
item.description: The jobs report is the first major economic data release since the midterms.

item.title: Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip with a first stop in Uruguay
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America on Friday, November 6, with a visit to Uruguay, the region’s least Catholic and most secular country, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question. After Uruguay, he will then go to Argentina and Peru. FRANCE 24's Hanna Roberts has more.

item.title: California governor to grant clemency to all 548 death row inmates in state
item.description: California's governor Gavy Newsom announced Thursday that he will commute all death sentences in the state to life without the possibility of parole. He said that "capital punishment is morally wrong." The state Supreme Court will have the final say in hundreds of those cases.

item.title: The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult is sentenced to 200 years in prison
item.description: Cult leader Paul Mackenzie was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult after he ordered his followers to starve themselves to death in order to meet Jesus. (Image credit: Brian Inganga)

item.title: Thomas Markle charged by FBI in Florida
item.description: The Duchess of Sussex's father, Thomas Markle Snr, has been charged by the FBI in Florida over child sexual abuse material.

item.title: Russell Brand's barrister reports himself to watchdog over behaviour after verdict
item.description: Russell Brand's barrister has reported himself to a professional regulator over a clash with a journalist after his client was convicted of rape.

item.title: The women who rode the blue wave
item.description: In this edition, we report on how the US midterms, which saw the Democrats make massive gains, also marked a series of historic firsts for women. Also the dark side to Bangkok's booming fertility industry, which attracts thousands of foreign patients seeking assistance from the Thai capital's state-of-the-art private clinics. Plus how an impoverished neighbourhood in El Salvador, once a no-go zone plagued by gang violence, is being transformed by women into a vibrant canvas for street art.

item.title: Ex-lawmaker gets 12.5 years in Macao's first national security case
item.description: Au's arrest last year was the first publicly known prosecution under Macao's national security law since it was enacted in 2009. (Image credit: Bertha Wang)

item.title: 'Too early to draw conclusions' as bomb threat hoaxes target European countries
item.description: Several Irish media outlets reported receiving bomb threats on Friday as a wave of hoax alerts that had so far mainly targeted airlines continued across Europe, with more than a dozen new flights affected. No explosives have been found in any of the incidents so far. European authorities are scrambling to identify the sources of the threats, as FRANCE 24's Brussels correspondent Dave Keating reports.

item.title: Paraguay's Peña offers resignation amid banking scandal, protests
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña submitted his resignation on Thursday, but Congress put it on hold as impeachment proceedings against him move forward. Peña is facing impeachment over a banking scandal that has affected millions of people and sparked protests, with thousands taking to the streets in recent days.

item.title: Met chief warns that 'policing will fail' without major reforms
item.description: Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley has warned that “policing will fail” without major reforms, including reducing the number of regional forces.

item.title: Trump’s stillborn diesel deal: Why Russian oil tankers are not heading to the US
item.description: The first oil tankers scheduled to deliver Russian diesel to the US under a deal between President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin have changed course and are no longer heading toward the US coast. It spells the end of an agreement announced with great fanfare before the midterms.

item.title: Is Israel opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot going to replace Benjamin Netanyahu?
item.description: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday, November 5, as the frontrunner to be tasked with forming a government. This comes after one of the two main parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish voters – a longtime ally of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition – declined to recommend any candidate for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky reports.

item.title: Double murderer given extra 22 years for historical sexual assaults
item.description: A former Royal Navy petty officer who is serving a life sentence for two murders has been jailed for a further 22 years for sexually assaulting three young naval recruits and a 14-year-old boy in the 1990s.

item.title: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future in question after midterms setback
item.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's future is in question after Tuesday's, November 3, midterms setback. On Thursday, November 5, he issued a video message vowing to fight efforts in Congress to impeach him and defending the ‌Iran war as “courageous and historic”. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.

item.title: Tech giants lose $1 trillion in one day after Democrats victory in midterms
item.description: Trillions of dollars have been wiped off the stock value of major tech firms in the US, Europe and Asia. Investors appear worried about the possibility of an AI slowdown and tougher regulation as Democrats won the midterms in the US. Some of the Democratic candidates had expressed their opposition to the data centres that are needed to power AI technology.

item.title: Canada PM Mark Carney unveils budget to strengthen economy
item.description: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled his first ever budget on November 5, which set out strong ambitions for greater economic independence from the US. The "Masters of our Destiny" budget also announced generous measures for parts of the economy affected by tariffs, setting aside 44 billion Canadian dollars for impacted businesses and workers.

item.title: Will Democratic Party introduce a new 'New Deal'? Key narrative must be 'focused on economic issues'
item.description: With Democrats poised to control both chambers of Congress, the party faces a defining challenge: how to constrain Donald Trump's presidency while carving out a path to the White House in 2028. For Ian Reifowitz, Distinguished Professor of History at SUNY Empire State University, the answer lies in drawing on the historical legacy of Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal coalition. Republicans, he argues, have progressively shifted electoral competition towards questions of identity, immigration and cultural conflict. Democrats, by contrast, must recover their traditional strength on economic security, affordability and everyday living standards. "These Democrats across the country ran on affordability." And that's how they must govern, explains Reifowitz.

item.title: 'Period of uncertainty: Trump is tormented, he's unstoppable, and he's desperate for immortality'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Craig Copetas, Greek-American author, international affairs columnist and editor at Türkiye Today and French Senator Hélène Conway-Mouret. “What you have is a tormented and unstable president who's desperate for immortality.” With this arresting assessment, Copetas captures what he considers the defining paradox of Donald Trump's presidency in the aftermath of the US midterm elections: a leader politically neutered at home but potentially emboldened on the international stage.

item.title: The human cost of recycling: Kenyan waste pickers put their health at risk
item.description: Two thousand tonnes of waste are dumped every day at the Dandora landfill site in the Kenyan capital Nairobi. An army of workers then rush in to recover recyclable materials, putting their own health at risk in the process. But however hard these unsung environmental heroes work, only 7 percent of the plastic can be recycled. Our correspondents report.

item.title: Two dead after bus carrying schoolchildren crashes in France, officials say
item.description: A seven-year-old girl and an 18-year-old boy have been killed after a bus crashed in eastern France, French authorities said.

item.title: 'He's got to go': Hakeem Jeffries calls for Hegseth's removal but stops short of impeachment
item.description: Speaking with Morning Edition , Hakeem Jeffries discussed ending the Iran war, holding Trump accountable and calls for new Democratic leadership, but offered few specifics on how Democrats would deliver. (Image credit: Kevin Dietsch)

item.title: Past White House adviser Raj Panjabi has written a playbook for 'living room' crises
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi is the author of Safer: A Playbook. His goal is to help people face a personal crisis — health, workplace, family conflicts — and "turn fear into action." (Image credit: Ben de la Cruz/NPR)

item.title: Europe's crisis of discontent: Student and cost-of-living protests spread across EU
item.description: A growing wave of discontent is sweeping across Europe. What began in France as student protests over deteriorating school conditions, teacher shortages and an education system under pressure has quickly grown into something much bigger: a groundswell of discontent over the rising cost of living, unaffordable housing and struggling public services.

item.title: Israel's Eisenkot claims 'progress' in coalition talks as opposition eases on ultra-Orthodox draft
item.description: Israeli opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot said on Friday he was making "significant progress" in forming a government to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as one of his possible coalition partners walked back demands that ultra-Orthodox Jews complete military service and signalled a willingness to hold talks with the community.

item.title: French 2027 presidential elections: Why Mélenchon is a Gen Z favourite
item.description: Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon is beloved by French youth, but also one of the country’s most controversial politicians. His encouragement of the youth protests sweeping through France months ahead of the presidential election has only made him more divisive. So, why is Mélenchon a Gen Z favourite? FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young supporters to find out.

item.title: WATCH: Multiple water rescues amid flood emergencies in the South
item.description: A flood emergency is underway across multiple states in the South – triggering dozens of water rescues in Florida, Georgia and Tennessee in the middle of the night.

item.title: Two men charged with murder after death of non-league footballer
item.description: Two men have been charged with murder after the death of a non-league footballer.

item.title: Premier League footballer sparks police operation after bow and arrow sighting
item.description: Newcastle United's Bosnian full-back Amar Dedic reportedly found himself at the centre of a major police response after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows in the countryside.

item.title: WATCH: These identical twin sisters speak at the same time
item.description: Danny New talks to identical twin sisters in Australia who are turning heads for their unique speech patterns.

item.title: Prison operator and health board admit criminal charges after death of inmate with COVID
item.description: A prison operator and an NHS health board have admitted criminal charges after the death of an imprisoned man who contracted COVID-19.

item.title: Midterms over, Democrats eye wide-open 2028 White House race
item.description: With the US midterms over, Democrats are turning to what could become one of their most crowded and unpredictable presidential primaries in decades, a 2028 contest ​likely to expose the party's divide over how to win back the White House. Despite their resounding victories on Tuesday, Democrats enter the 2028 campaign still divided over whether to tack to the center or move further left on issues ranging from healthcare and taxes to policing and foreign policy.

item.title: Israel president to announce Sunday who will form new government
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday, November 8, whom he will task with trying to form a new government, following post-election talks with all party leaders. 46 parliament members recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, while 67 backed his opponent Gadi Eisenkot. Seven lawmakers abstained.

item.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: Vance says they lost the midterms because of ____
item.description: Plus: Heidi Klum's hand, hackers and the pope's visitor!

item.title: Why public schools nationwide are facing a massive drop in student enrollment
item.description: School enrollment was already expected to plunge by 2 million kids by 2030. Education experts say deporting immigrant families, many with school-age children, is making the crisis worse. (Image credit: Carlos Jaramillo for NPR)

item.title: Two teenagers in court - with one accused of attempted murder - after five seriously injured at Halloween party
item.description: Two 16-year-olds have appeared in court after five boys were seriously injured at a party on Halloween.

item.title: Left-leaning Washington, Colorado join conservative states in banning trans athletes
item.description: Voters in Washington and Colorado have approved measures to ban transgender athletes from participating in school sports

item.title: Data centers took a beating in the midterm elections
item.description: Opposition to data centers was part of midterm races across the U.S., with campaigns featuring them in hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of TV ads and many winners pledging to clamp down on the energy-hungry behemoths

item.title: WATCH: Authorities reveal motive in Citibank complex shooting
item.description: Chilling surveillance video shows a gunman exchanging gunfire with a security guard after ramming a gate at a Citibank complex near Tampa and killing a woman having lunch, authorities say.

item.title: WATCH: Meet the man who's the new voice of Boston's Logan airport
item.description: Christopher Donisi, an HVAC pipe fitter, will be the man behind the first voice travelers hear when they land in Beantown in the near future.

item.title: WATCH: Jaguars face injury-ravaged Ravens in Thursday Night Football matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler previews the Jaguars-Ravens matchup, Baltimore’s quarterback injuries and Trevor Lawrence’s strong start to the season.

item.title: WATCH: Bob Dylan, Prince William, Prince Harry: Here's what's trending
item.description: ABC News' Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including Bob Dylan meeting with Pope Leo at the Vatican and Prince William and Prince Harry joining forces to honor their mother.

item.title: Who won the redistricting war? So far, it looks like Democrats
item.description: Dems were able to keep seats that Republicans redrew to make them GOP-friendly.

item.title: Dow plunges 1,800 points, wiping out gains from midterm results rally
item.description: The selloff came a day after the Dow soared more than 1,500 points.

item.title: 'Extinction-level event': How Republicans eyeing 2028 are taking midterm losses
item.description: Republicans considering a presidential run offered their assessment of the party's performance in the midterm elections.

item.title: Judge blasts administration for planning to deport Iranians to Iran during wartime
item.description: The Trump administration said during a hearing that it's been making plans to deport Iranian migrants back to Iran during the war, earning a rebuke from a federal judge.

item.title: Breakaway league LIV Golf to fold after filing for bankruptcy
item.description: Breakaway men's league LIV Golf is to fold instead of launching a new version because of a lack of financial support.

item.title: Family of footballer who died after on-pitch collision pay tribute to him
item.description: Family, friends and teammates gathered for the funeral of the Spanish footballer who died following an on-field collision with another player.

item.title: Meghan's brother a 'person of interest' in child abuse image claims
item.description: Meghan Markle's half brother has been named as a "person of interest" in an investigation into child sexual abuse image allegations against the Duchess of Sussex's father.

item.title: Trump says he has 'every intention' to keep Hegseth
item.description: President Donald Trump said he intends to keep Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in his job, as Rep. Massie, prepares to introduce an impeachment resolution against him.

item.description: Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, explains what's behind the decrease in prices.

item.description: A Citibank employee was shot and killed at a business complex in Florida on Wednesday, according to local authorities and company officials.

item.description: ABC News’ Tom Soufi Burridge reports from Paris, where tens of thousands of police officers have been deployed to help maintain law and order.

item.title: WATCH: The wide-ranging reactions to election night
item.description: After an Election Day so pivotal that votes were even being cast from space, there were many expressive reactions shared online.

item.description: Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football. Pic: AP

item.description: A student-run automotive shop has opened to the public – giving high schoolers hands-on experience with oil changes, tire rotations and multi-point inspections.

item.description: ABC News political contributors Amanda Renteria, a Democratic strategist, and Ramesh Ponnuru, editor of the National Review, share more about what's being called a "blue tsunami."
